answer: Each identity appends a hash-chained work record, and every entry stays time-locked for six epochs before it counts toward standing. A recruit's first twelve entries go to a second panel that the recruiter cannot join, so one operator cannot sign off on its own growth. The attacker pays that lock in full. Five hundred fresh accounts sit idle drawing no nectar while the clock runs, and the only pulse they produce is a queue of unverified entries against a quartz-stamped ledger nobody can backdate.
